value.doc: One run of the LRR calculation, for the institution as a whole.
The institution's PLA supervisory category, which sets its scaling factor.
MIN [ Stressed inflows, .70 × Stressed outflows ].
Inflow cap factor: inflows count up to .70 of stressed outflows (LRR Calculation).

LRR = Stock of eligible liquid assets / Net stressed outflows, as a fraction (1.25 = 125%),
rounded half to even at four decimal places (a percentage to two decimal places); zero when
there are no net stressed outflows.
Minimum Requirement: the LRR is at least 110 percent.
Minimum LRR: 110 percent (Minimum Requirement).

Net stressed outflows = Scaling factor × [ stressed outflows − capped inflows +
concentration add-on ].
Scaling Factor Table: the factor for each supervisory category.

Stressed outflows: the retail outflows calculated here plus the other outflows reported
from slices not yet modeled.

The Liquidity Resilience Ratio (Rule 14, LRR Calculation): the stock of eligible liquid
assets over net stressed outflows.

One LRR calculation brings together amounts from the rest of the policy and amounts reported
from elsewhere. The stock of eligible liquid assets and the retail outflows are calculated by
this model's rules; the other outflows, the inflows and the concentration add-on come from
slices not yet modeled and are reported.
The larger of an amount and zero.

(14.6) Eligible Liquid Assets: the asset's code is in Tier 1, 2 or 3 and it is under
liquidity desk control.
Excess over tier limits = Tier 2 and 3 limit excess + Tier 3 limit excess.

Stock of eligible liquid assets = Tier 1 + .80 × Tier 2 + .40 × Tier 3 − excess over tier
limits.
The asset's market value when it counts toward Tier 1, else zero.
Tier 1 value: total market value of the eligible Tier 1 assets.
Tier 2 and 3 limit excess = MAX[ 0, .80 × Tier 2 + .40 × Tier 3 − .8182 × Tier 1 ].
Tier 2 and 3 limit factor: .8182 of Tier 1, so Tiers 2 and 3 are at most 45% of the stock.
The asset's market value when it counts toward Tier 2, else zero.
Tier 2 value: total market value of the eligible Tier 2 assets.
Tier 2 weight: .80 (LRR Calculation).

Tier 3 limit excess = MAX[ 0, .40 × Tier 3 − Tier 2 and 3 limit excess
− .1111 × (Tier 1 + .80 × Tier 2) ].

Tier 3 limit factor: .1111 of Tier 1 and weighted Tier 2, so Tier 3 is at most 10% of the
stock.
The asset's market value when it counts toward Tier 3, else zero.
Tier 3 value: total market value of the eligible Tier 3 assets.
Tier 3 weight: .40 (LRR Calculation).
Overview: the tier an asset counts toward, or NotEligible when rule 14.6 excludes it.

The stock of eligible liquid assets, the LRR numerator (Rule 14, LRR Calculation), from
L.1 unrestricted assets selected by rule 14.6.
The Rule 14 outflow rule a balance falls under.

(14.21) Guaranteed Core Retail Deposits: R.1 and R.2, Retail or Small Business, covered in
full by the NDGS.

(14.24) Intermediated Retail Deposits: R.4, Retail or Small Business, whatever the
guarantee.
R.1 Transaction Accounts or R.2 Relationship Savings Accounts: the core retail products.
(14.25) Other Retail Balances: R.5, Retail or Small Business.

Overview: the first of rules 14.21 to 14.25 a balance matches. A balance from a
counterparty other than Retail or Small Business falls under none of them.

(14.23) Rate-Seeking Retail Deposits: R.3, Retail or Small Business, whatever the
guarantee.

Run-off rate for each rule, as a fraction of the balance (rules 14.21 to 14.25). Balances
outside these rules are covered by wholesale rules not in scope, so no outflow is computed
for them here.
Stressed outflow for one balance: balance times its rule's run-off rate, to the cent.
Total stressed retail outflows across all Part R records.

(14.22) Unguaranteed Core Retail Deposits: R.1 and R.2, Retail or Small Business, covered
by a foreign scheme or unguaranteed.
Rule 14 retail outflow rules 14.21 to 14.25, applied to Part R records.

Asset codes from Schedule B. An `E` suffix means the asset meets all the asset-specific
tests of Rule 14.6.
The tier of the stock of eligible liquid assets an asset code belongs to.

Schedule B: which tier each asset code is in. Codes without the `E` suffix fail the Rule
14.6 tests, and municipal debt is never eligible.
The Asset Code field: the code of Schedule B, the asset code table.
The Form PL-7 counterparty types, in the order the instructions list them.

Retail (a natural person) or Small Business (an entity managed as a retail exposure):
the counterparties every retail outflow rule, 14.21 to 14.25, applies to.

Form PL-7 field definition: Counterparty. The type of legal counterparty that placed a
balance (not its ultimate parent).
Whether a balance is covered in full, and by which scheme.

Covered in full by the National Deposit Guarantee Scheme. Only NDGS coverage counts as
guaranteed for Rule 14; a foreign scheme is treated as unguaranteed.

Form PL-7 field definition: Guarantee. Whether a balance is covered in full by a
government deposit guarantee scheme.
One reported line of L.1: Unrestricted Assets.
Form PL-7 Part L: Liquid Assets, product L.1: Unrestricted Assets.

The Part R products:

  - R.1: Transaction Accounts
  - R.2: Relationship Savings Accounts
  - R.3: Rate-Seeking Savings Accounts
  - R.4: Intermediated Deposits
  - R.5: Other Retail Balances
One record in Part R. `balance` is in millions of FCR.
Form PL-7 Part R: Retail Deposits.
